next_steps: Redwood to send updated co-sell playbook deck with pricing tiers and sample statements of work
Schedule 30m tech benchmark next week for top 3 joint opportunities (SE-led)
Jupiter to confirm list of 6 priority accounts and intro contacts by 2026-12-15
action_items: Samira Patel: send updated co-sell playbook deck: 2026-12-13
Ethan Cho: prepare benchmark plan and test script for latency/cost comparison: 2026-12-17
Priya Desai (Jupiter): share standard SOW redlines and security checklist: 2026-12-16
Nate Brown (Jupiter): finalize 6 priority accounts list and provide contacts: 2026-12-15
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-12-11 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Nate Brown (Jupiter Head of Partnerships), Leah Kim (Jupiter Cloud Architect), Omar Ruiz (Jupiter Sales Director), Priya Desai (Jupiter Legal)
summary: Quarter-end channel sync to triage joint opportunities and align on an executive-facing co-sell playbook. Focus on three deals that could be accelerated with an exec-led pilot, clarify responsibilities for joint benchmarks, and confirm legal/security gating items for pilots in regulated accounts.
topics: 1) Deal triage and prioritization; 2) Playbook and collateral updates (exec hooks); 3) Technical benchmark scope and success metrics; 4) Security/legal pre-reqs for pilot; 5) Next steps and owner matrix
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give folks a minute. um Nate, thanks for pulling the team together.
[00:18] Nate: yeah thanks Samira, appreciate it. quick note — we have a hard push on Q4 targets so want to see which of the joint opps we can actually land before the holidays.
[00:32] Ethan: perfect, we'll go through the three priority opps that Samira sent over and flag tech risks vs exec-level plays.
[00:46] Leah: quick clarifying q — when you say pilot, do you mean a Redwood hosted pilot or private deployment inside our customer's VPC? we have a couple that require VPC-only.
[01:03] Samira: good q — typically we do a hosted Redwood API pilot for speed, but for regulated ones we can do Redwood Private (sorry sometimes our notes say Redwood Privatee) in a dedicated VPC. depends on their security ask.
[01:18] Omar: right, for AcmeCorp the SI says they need KMS integration and audit logs. is that covered?
[01:29] Ethan: yes, we can integrate with customer KMS, and the platform provides audit logs — low-level fields are possible, though we may need a quick config pass. there sometimes is confusion with SAML provisioning — so we should confirm identity flow.
[01:45] Priya: from legal side i'll need the standard SOC two and contract redlines. we can't accept some of the long-tail data retention clauses without review.
[01:55] Maya: noted — we'll attach the SOC 2 report and the security checklist. Samira will share the doc.
[02:10] Samira: ok, jumping into opps. first, "Nimbus Retail" — $420k ACV potential, procurement window ~Q1. They already trialed a competitor (Cloudbox AI) and had latency concerns.
[02:28] Nate: Nimbus is interesting, they care a lot about 95th percentile latency. their sales contact is Maria Chen.
[02:38] Ethan: for Nimbus we should run a top-line latency/cost bench — we can show continuous batching benefits and KV cache improvements. i'll propose a test script.
[02:51] Leah: what sequence lengths are relevant? Nimbus uses long chat sessions ~2k tokens — need to verify.
[03:03] Ethan: ok i'll default to sequences of 512, 1024, and a 2k spike to represent their tail. we'll measure p95 and p99 and token cost.
[03:16] Omar: second opp is "HelioMed" — regulated healthcare account. much smaller ACV but fast pilot potential. they insisted on private deployment.
[03:29] Samira: this is where Redwood Private comes in — we'll need an on-prem or VPC checklist. Priya, can you share your security redlines?
[03:40] Priya: yes i'll send the baseline, but HelioMed requires an additional audit window and retention constraints.
[03:50] Ethan: for HelioMed we might suggest a short canary: dedicated infra, minimal feature set, and strict data retention. that reduces scope and legal friction.
[04:02] Nate: third opp is a strategic account "Atlas Finance" — large, procurement cycle is long but if we get an exec intro it's high value. they asked about pricing freedom vs committed capacity.
[04:16] Samira: on Atlas we should propose a hybrid: start hosted to prove concept, then move to Dedicated once they commit. that helps reduce the upfront infra lift.
[04:28] Omar: Atlas also asked about model explainability and audit trails — anything built-in?
[04:35] Ethan: we have trace-level outputs in console and token-level cost breakdowns — but we don't currently surface a turn-by-turn explainability report; we can produce structured logs for audits though.
[04:48] Leah: i'll need to know retention defaults so i can map them to their compliance regs.
[04:55] Maya: we'll include a table in the playbook that maps retention/regions/controls by deployment mode.
[05:06] Samira: ok moving to playbook — we updated exec slides to include three hooks: business outcome, quick win pilot, and risk mitigation. feedback?
[05:20] Nate: love the hooks. can we add a one-pager for execs: TL;DR value, timeline, ask (CRO intro or proof-of-concept signoff).
[05:31] Samira: yes — i'll add a 1-page executive ask template.
[05:36] Priya: legal wants any exec ask to be non-binding; make sure the language is clear.
[05:41] Samira: noted.
[05:44] Ethan: for bench scope, here's the rough plan: 1) baseline: run their sample prompt through Redwood hosted and competitor (Cloudbox AI), 2) latency distribution p50/p95/p99, 3) cost per 1k tokens estimate, 4) qualitative eval on hallucinations for prompt set.
[06:05] Leah: sample prompt sets — Nimbus can provide 40 prompts, Atlas has 20, HelioMed will give redacted clinical flows.
[06:16] Ethan: perfect. whoever owns the account can push those prompts into the folder we'll share.
[06:22] Omar: timeline? you mentioned next week for bench?
[06:25] Ethan: yeah aim to run bench next Wed-Thu window — we'll need access creds and a short API key from the customer or a sandbox. for VPC tests we'll need networking windows.
[06:38] Samira: action owner matrix: Samira leads exec playbook, Ethan leads tech bench, Maya handles comms and collateral, Jupiter to provide contacts and legal redlines.
[06:52] Nate: sounds good. one risk — Inferex recently did a pitch to Nimbus; they emphasized lower token cost but had worse p95. we should call that out tactically.
[07:06] Ethan: yep we'll include competitor data row: cost vs latency tradeoff.
[07:12] Priya: legal Q — can Redwood provide a list of subprocessors and data flow diagrams? we need that for HelioMed's security team.
[07:22] Samira: yes we'll include subprocessors doc and a basic data flow diagram.
[07:30] Leah: also need clarification on KMS integration — is it full BYOK or envelope encryption?
[07:36] Ethan: we support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) for the private deployment path; for hosted we have envelope options. i'll detail in the security checklist.
[07:48] Omar: pricing conversation — if Atlas wants committed capacity, how flexible is the discounting?
[07:56] Samira: we have tiered reserved capacity pricing; a small reserved pool can be trialed with a conversion clause. i'll share sample pricing tiers in the deck.
[08:08] Nate: one ask from execs — can you provide a 30-minute "value story" session for Atlas execs? their CRO wants an example revenue model with LTV uplift.
[08:20] Samira: yes we can do an executive briefing; Maya will draft the value story and Samira will present.
[08:28] Maya: i'll pull 2 customer case studies and a one-pager LTV uplift model.
[08:34] Ethan: technical note: for the latency bench we need to ensure tokenization parity with the customer's pipeline — sometimes tokenizers produce differences that skew cost numbers.
[08:47] Leah: good call — Nimbus uses a custom tokenizer in prod, we'll provide mapping.
[08:53] Samira: ok let's talk gating items for pilots — legal, security, network, and an executive sponsor. which of these are blockers for Nimbus?
[09:05] Nate: exec sponsor is in place, network is minor, legal wants SOC two and subprocessors list, security wants KMS details. so mostly docs.
[09:16] Priya: i'll send HelioMed's non-negotiables, but for Nimbus standard checklist should be fine.
[09:23] Samira: good. moving to the 6-account list — Nate will confirm.
[09:29] Nate: yes i'll confirm and share contacts by 12/15.
[09:33] Ethan: related — for the tech bench we should pick 3 representative prompts and run them across three model variants, include a quantized variant to show cost delta.
[09:45] Omar: do we need to worry about model drift or evals after initial pilot?
[09:50] Ethan: we propose post-pilot quality monitoring via Redwood Optimize — we can set regression alerts by prompt set.
[09:58] Maya: i'll add that to the playbook as 'quality guardrails'.
[10:03] Samira: ok any procurement/legal timeline issues?
[10:07] Priya: from Jupiter side legal we'll need a 2-week review once we get SOW, so plan lead times accordingly.
[10:14] Samira: got it. i'll include contingency in dates.
[10:19] Nate: one final tactical — for the executive ask, can you provide a one-slide ROI example for Atlas showing 6-12 month payback?
[10:29] Samira: yes, we'll draft it and put numbers based on assumed uplift + cost per 1k.
[10:35] Ethan: small nit — when we compare competitors, ensure we use the same token counting rules. Cloudbox sometimes reports tokens differently.
[10:46] Leah: will do.
[10:48] Omar: any other blockers?
[10:50] Nate: none here.
[10:52] Samira: recap: Samira to send playbook + pricing tiers by 12/13; Ethan to publish bench plan and test script by 12/17; Priya to send security redlines and SOW asks by 12/16; Nate to provide 6 priority accounts & contacts by 12/15. schedule bench window for 12/16-18.
[11:15] Priya: i'll also flag anything that requires additional legal review.
[11:22] Maya: i'll coordinate calendars and set the benchmark meetings.
[11:30] Samira: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links to docs (playbook deck, security checklist, test folder).
[11:40] Nate: thanks team, excited to push these.
[11:44] Ethan: thanks all. bye.
[11:46] END TRANSCRIPT
